messages.author: e5c7e56038437512
messages.subject: Alternative parameterization for SPDE method
parts:
Hi!

I hope all you are well in this complex situation (COVID 19)
I have been having problems to obtain good posterior estimations for the hyperparameters related with SPDE method. 
I know that the SPDE method use 'ln_tau' and 'ln_kappa' to obtain a Q matrix but the interpretability of this parameters are very complex because in INLA these are 'internal' parameters of this method and with a normal prior distribution. I was reading the paper of Lindgren and Rue, 2015 and they propose use the 'practical_range' (rho) and 'marginal_variance' (sigma) to parameterize the SPDE.
Someone have any idea for this?

This is an example of my code in TMB

// Hyperpriors
   Type tau     = exp(ln_tau);
   Type kappa = exp(ln_kappa);
   
   nlp -= dnorm(tau,           Type(0.0),   Type(2.0), true);
   nlp -= dnorm(kappa,      Type(12.0), Type(2.0), true);

and this is the values in the 'data' parameters in R
             ln_tau      = spde$param.inla$theta.initial[1],                                                  
             ln_kappa = spde$param.inla$theta.initial[2]

beforehand thank you very much
Regards

messages.author: 0965a429193e691b
messages.subject: Re: Alternative parameterization for SPDE method
parts:
Hi,
If you're looking at this paper https://www.stat.washington.edu/peter/591/Lindgren.pdf the marginal variance is described in equation 2 , and  rho can be inferred from equation 5 in terms of kappa.  you could code them to be output like this:


Type range = sqrt(8)/kappa;   //Distance at which correlation has dropped to 0.1
Type  marginal_variance = pow(exp(.5*log(Type(1.0)/(Type(4.0)*M_PI)) - ln_kappa - ln_tau),2);


Assuming alpha=2, and your spatial data is 2-d (d=2).
